svg.aria-label: Rail routing on the solder side of the RPI-BC input board. The plus-14-volt rail runs straight through the row of twelve resistor leads. The Pi ground rail and the 24 volt COM rail each run in a free row offset from the pins they serve, with a short stub to each target, because along a DIP top edge the pins alternate collector and emitter and along a connector only pin 4 is COM.

g.text: SOLDER SIDE — all three rails live here
Socket pads are only reachable from this side, so the ground rail has no choice; the other two follow it for one convention.
Pi header + fan-out — pad↔GPIO map must be rung out
Pi GND rail — free row, 12 stubs
top edge alternates C E C E — a rail along the pin row would short every phototransistor
+14 V rail — straight through, because you place its targets
dashed = insulated cathode runs; they cross the bare rail freely
24 V COM rail — free row, 4 stubs to pin 4 only
pins 1–3 are channels — a rail along this row would short every one to COM
rails bare · runs insulated · sleeve only where a rail crosses a rail
